messages.subject: similarity measure
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

does anybody know a mean to compare two networks created with deal on
different data sets (continuous and discret), i.e. with uncomparable
scores? I could imagine a function in the deal package or another
package in R which calculates a kind of similarity score between two
networks by calculating the number of steps needed to convert one
network into the other by adding, turning or removing arcs. I would be
thankful for any ideas or hints.

Marit

messages.subject: positive network logscore
messages.body_plain:
Hi all, I'm a newbie and I'm using deal since 1 week, so sorry if my 
question is a little bit stupid. With the dataset I'm analysing, deal 
returns me a positive network logscore. Do you have an idea of why 
this happens? My network has 9 nodes, 1 discrete+8 continuous. I've 
checked the logscore of all nodes, and 5 of them are positive. I guess 
this is because the data are far from being linear dependent, since 
I've made a linear regression and the pvalue of the residuals is 1e-
15. 
Thank, 
       Stefano Castruccio

messages.subject: SV: positive network logscore
messages.body_plain:
Stefano
 
(I've copied the following from another answer)
 
The score should not be positive, so something is not right here. This is
possibly caused by numerical instabilities, either because the jointprior has a
too low size of the imaginary database, or because the continuous variables need
to be rescaled. If, for example, you have a continuous variable taking values
around 0.001, try multiplying the variable by 1000.

I have not explored this further, so I have not got a really good explanation
for what is going on.

Best,
Claus
